findings.passage: Whereas approximately 11 percent of American citizens lack government-issued photo identification, and a disproportionate number are low-income, elderly, or people of color;
findings.note: Text of the House resolution Norton introduced on 2019-11-18, published on her official site. It lists the share of citizens lacking photo ID as a reason for the resolution, which condemns restrictive state voting laws.

findings.passage: Whereas many voting-eligible, low-income Latino voters are naturalized United States citizens who lack proof of citizenship and cannot afford a Certificate of Citizenship or a Replacement Certificate of Naturalization, which cost $1,170 and $555, respectively;
findings.note: Same resolution text. It raises cost and access problems for naturalized citizens who must show proof of citizenship.

findings.passage: Whereas, 15 states will implement new voting restrictions such as burdensome photo identification requirements and reduced early voting hours for the 2016 presidential election for the first time;
findings.note: Text of a resolution Norton announced on 2016-08-09, published on her official site. It describes state photo ID requirements as burdensome.

findings.passage: Whereas, more than 21 million Americans lack government-issued photo ID and a disproportionate number of those Americans are low-income, elderly, or people of color;
findings.note: Same resolution text, on how many Americans lack a government photo ID.

findings.passage: However, voter fraud is practically non-existent in the United States.
findings.note: Statement in her official press release, issued as Ranking Member before a House Oversight subcommittee hearing on immigration actions and elections. She calls voter fraud claims unfounded.
